paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyse continuum and molecular emission, observed with ALMA, from the dust-enshrouded intermediate-mass AGB star OH 30.1 −0.7.
We present here a complete molecular inventory of the existing ALMA data of OH 30.1 −0.7 (also known as V1362 Aql, IRAS 18460 –0254, AFGL 5535), where previously only CO observations were published.

question.value: What is the complete molecular inventory and circumstellar structure of the intermediate-mass AGB star OH 30.1-0.7, and what does its circumstellar chemistry reveal about a potential binary companion and mass-loss history?

evidence.quote: Thus far, no studies of the circumstellar chemistry of confirmed intermediate-mass AGB stars have been presented.
In Sect. 3 we present the detected molecular lines and discuss the implications of these results in Sect. 4, in particular how these observations support the presence of a companion star.
OH 30.1 −0.7 was observed with two ALMA receivers, Bands 3 and 6, in 2016 and 2017, as part of project 2016.1.00005.S.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00005.S.
OH 30.1 −0.7 was observed with two ALMA receivers, Bands 3 and 6, in 2016 and 2017, as part of project 2016.1.00005.S.

claims.hypothesis: OH 30.1-0.7 hosts an unseen main-sequence binary companion in its inner wind that is hotter than a red dwarf (G-type or hotter) but not hotter than a late B-type star (< 12000 K).
claims.experiment: Map the spatial distribution of NS and measure the rotational and vibrational transitions of NaCl and KCl with ALMA Bands 3 and 6, comparing with circumstellar photochemical and neutral-neutral reaction constraints.
claims.result: NS is detected asymmetrically out to 1.8" along an axis perpendicular to feature B, while NaCl (up to v=4) and KCl (up to v=2) are strongly detected with T ~ 600 K in the inner wind.
claims.finding: UV photons from a G-type or hotter companion are required to photodissociate N2 to form NS, whereas a companion hotter than ~12000 K (late B-type) would photoionise Na and K into unreactive closed-shell ions and prevent NaCl and KCl formation.

evidence.quote: We find that the NS emission is off centre and arranged along an axis perpendicular to the direction of feature B, indicative of a UV-emitting binary companion (e.g. a G-type main sequence star or hotter), perhaps on an eccentric orbit, contributing to its formation.
However, the NaCl and KCl emission constrain the nature of that companion to not be hotter than a late B-type main sequence star.

We conclude that a companion star hotter than around ∼ 12000 K would cause too much photoionisation of Na and K to reconcile our observations, unless densities are very high in that region of the wind.

claims.hypothesis: The secondary continuum source 'feature B' is cold, ice-coated dust ejecta associated with OH 30.1-0.7 rather than an unrelated background object.
claims.experiment: Image continuum in ALMA Bands 3 and 6 across compact and extended configurations, measure the spectral index of feature B, and compare its position with the morphology of the CO envelope and NS emission axis.
claims.result: Feature B is detected at >10 sigma in Band 6 at 4.6" (1.8e4 au) separation with a bridge of faint continuum emission connecting it to the primary peak, a spectral index >3.6, alignment with an indentation in the CO envelope, and an axis perpendicular to the NS major axis.
claims.finding: Feature B is most likely cold, ice-coated dust ejecta associated with the AGB star, though a background source in W43 cannot be completely ruled out.

evidence.quote: This feature is most likely composed of cold dust and is likely to be ejecta associated with the AGB star, though we cannot rule out that it is a background object.
In the compact Band 6 data, there appears to be a bridge connecting the primary and secondary peaks, traces of which are seen in the combined and extended continuum data in Fig. 1.
The fact that the extent of the NS emission lies perpendicular to the projected separation between the AGB star and feature B lends some weight to this scenario.

claims.hypothesis: The outer edge of the CO envelope around OH 30.1-0.7 marks the onset of a high mass-loss phase ~2800 years ago rather than steady-state photodissociation truncation of a continuous high-density wind.
claims.experiment: Compare the angular extents and edge steepness of CO J=2-1 and J=1-0 emission in ALMA channel maps and zeroth moment maps.
claims.result: CO J=2-1 and J=1-0 have the same outer angular extent (~3.5" or 14,000 au at matched resolution) with a sharp drop-off in both spatial contours and extreme velocity channels; at v_exp = 23 km/s, this corresponds to 2800 years.
claims.finding: High mass-loss commenced around 2800 years ago (longer than classical superwind predictions), and any earlier mass loss at a rate <= 2e-5 M_sun/yr would have already photodissociated at smaller radii.

evidence.quote: The CO emission is abruptly truncated around 3 . 5 ′′ or 14,000 au from the continuum peak, suggesting that mass loss at a high rate may have commenced as little as 2800 years ago.

Our observations reveal a very steep drop off at the edges of the CO emission, both in the plane of the sky and in velocity space. This suggests that the bounds of the CO envelope are not truncated by the interstellar radiation field, as is usually the case.
Essentially, any earlier mass-loss at this rate or lower would not be detectable, because that CO would have photodissociated before expanding to larger radii.

why_this_data.value: Existing ALMA Band 3 and 6 observations of OH 30.1-0.7 had only been published for CO previously; a full molecular inventory of a confirmed intermediate-mass AGB star had never been presented, and ALMA's spatial filtering mitigates severe single-dish ISM contamination from W43.

evidence.quote: Thus far, no studies of the circumstellar chemistry of confirmed intermediate-mass AGB stars have been presented.
We present here a complete molecular inventory of the existing ALMA data of OH 30.1 −0.7 (also known as V1362 Aql, IRAS 18460 –0254, AFGL 5535), where previously only CO observations were published.

ALMA has an advantage because, although the ALMA field of view can be similar to the half-power beam width (HPBW) of a single antenna, the interferometer acts as a spatial filter, resolving out smooth large-scale emission, including that from large molecular clouds.

why_this_method.value: Additional self-calibration improved dynamic range over standard archive products; Gaussian uv-tapering on combined Band 6 continuum reduced long-baseline sparse-sampling artefacts; convolving Band 3 continuum to the Band 6 compact beam enabled direct spectral index comparison; multi-radius aperture extraction ensured both compact and extended shell-like lines were detected.

evidence.quote: Rather than using the data products from the standard ALMA pipeline, we performed an additional self-calibration for OH 30.1 −0.7.
To mitigate this we applied a Gaussian taper to the visibility weights as a function of projected baseline length to reduce the weight of data from the longest baselines.
Spectra were extracted for apertures of different radii to ensure that lines excited in different parts of the circumstellar envelope were not overlooked.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Feature B as a coincidental background source (e.g., in W43 at 5.5 kpc) or foreground source rather than AGB ejecta.

evidence.quote: It is possible that feature B is a coincident background (or foreground) source. Given the line of sight proximity of OH 30.1 −0.7 to the star-forming region W43, that is the most likely origin of background sources.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Feature B as a hot UV-emitting companion star causing the CO indentation via localised photodissociation; rejected as unlikely because it is difficult to reconcile with the cold ice-coated dust implied by its steep spectral index (>3.6) and lack of optical/UV detection.

evidence.quote: Another possibility is that feature B is causing the indentation through non-gravitational means, perhaps through high energy UV photons, although this is difficult to reconcile with the cold dust implied by the spectral index.

Counter to this and unlike a companion located within the dust envelope of OH 30.1 −0.7, it is unclear why such a UV source would be too attenuated to be detected from Earth but not too attenuated to affect the OH 30.1 −0.7 CO envelope. Or why such a hot source would not destroy ice-covered dust grains.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Heating by UV photons alone driving NaCl and KCl formation; rejected because UV photons would be strongly attenuated by dust or would photoionise Na and K into unreactive closed-shell ions, preventing chloride formation.

evidence.loc: C5.1 The formation of NaCl and KCl
evidence.quote: For this reason, heating from UV photons alone is unlikely to drive the formation of NaCl or KCl since the UV photons will be highly attenuated and, if they were not, they would instead ionise the metals and prevent the formation of NaCl and KCl.

limitations_admitted.value: Severe interstellar CO contamination from the background star-forming region W43 persists in ALMA channels below ~100 km/s, preventing analysis of the blue side of CO J=1-0 and causing missing circumstellar emission at 84.1 km/s in CO J=2-1.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, some contamination persists, as can be seen in our CO channel maps in Figs. 3 and A6.
For the 𝐽 = 1 − 0 emission we only integrate over the red part of the CO line (i.e. for 𝜐 ≥ 101 . 7 km s −1 ) because the ISM contamination is too large and confounds the data at lower velocities.

limitations_admitted.value: Angular resolution (~0.3" in Band 6, ~1.3" in Band 3) is insufficient to spatially resolve the NaCl and KCl emitting regions (~0.014" or 50 au) or the inner binary companion separation, and only marginally resolves NS in Band 3.

evidence.quote: The zeroth moment map in Fig. 9 shows that the NS emission is mostly located to the east and north of OH 30.1 −0.7, and is only marginally spatially resolved.
As can be seen in Fig. 11, the KCl lines are not spatially resolved.
From our estimate of the average salt extent, we predict that observations with an angular resolution of 5 mas or better are required to resolve the structures in the inner wind.

limitations_admitted.value: Uneven spectral coverage misses the main isotopologue 28Si32S, 12C35Cl/Na35Cl v=0, SiO, HCN, SO, and matched isotopologue transition pairs of SO2, precluding isotopic ratio analyses and full radiative transfer modelling in this work.

evidence.quote: Our spectral coverage of SiS is uneven and misses lines from the most abundant isotopologue, 28 Si 32 S (hereafter we drop the isotope labels for 28 Si and 32 S). Therefore, although we detect several lines from isotopologues of SiS, we do not perform an analysis of isotopic ratios in this work.
We do not calculate isotopic ratios here because we do not clearly detect any two pairs of lines with the same quantum numbers across isotopologues.

referee_caveats_inferred: Population diagrams for NaCl and KCl assume LTE and optically thin emission without full non-LTE radiative transfer modelling or infrared radiative pumping corrections, which can strongly affect vibrationally excited states (up to v=4) in dusty inner winds.
The SO2 excitation temperature constraint (<= 25 K) is based on a single non-detected transition (E_low = 111 K) under LTE assumptions rather than non-LTE excitation modelling.

Constraints on the spectral type of the putative binary companion rely on qualitative comparisons with chemical models developed for other AGB stars rather than a dedicated chemical/hydrodynamical model tailored to OH 30.1-0.7.
